title: Asr prayer
intro: The third daily prayer: 4 sunnah and 4 fard – 8 rak‘ahs.

learn.html: Asr is the third daily prayer. Its time is in the middle of the time between Dhuhr (midday) and sunset. It has 8 rak‘ahs: four sunnah and four fard. We pray the sunnah first, then the fard.

learn.label: Niyyah for the sunnah of Asr
learn.ar: نَوَيْتُ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى صَلَاةَ سُنَّةِ الْعَصْرِ أَدَاءً مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
learn.tr: Nawaytu an usalliya lillaahi ta‘aalaa salaata sunnatil-‘asri, adaa’an mustaqbilal-qiblati. Allaahu akbar!
learn.en: I intend to pray, for Allah, the sunnah of Asr, on time, facing the Qiblah. Allah is the Greatest!

items: 1st rak‘ah: Subhanaka, A‘udhu, Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah
2nd rak‘ah: Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah
First sitting: At-Tahiyyat and the salawat
3rd rak‘ah: Subhanaka, Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah
4th rak‘ah: Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah
Last sitting: At-Tahiyyat, salawat, duas and salam

learn.title: 💡 Look closely
learn.html: In the sunnah of Asr, the first sitting has At-Tahiyyat and the salawat, and the 3rd rak‘ah starts again with Subhanaka. In the Dhuhr sunnah it was different!

learn.label: Niyyah for the fard of Asr
learn.ar: نَوَيْتُ أَنْ أُصَلِّيَ لِلَّهِ تَعَالَى صَلَاةَ فَرْضِ الْعَصْرِ أَدَاءً مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ، اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
learn.tr: Nawaytu an usalliya lillaahi ta‘aalaa salaata fardil-‘asri, adaa’an mustaqbilal-qiblati. Allaahu akbar!
learn.en: I intend to pray, for Allah, the fard of Asr, on time, facing the Qiblah. Allah is the Greatest!

items: 1st rak‘ah: Subhanaka, A‘udhu, Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah
2nd rak‘ah: Bismillah, Al-Fatiha and a surah
Last sitting: At-Tahiyyat, salawat, duas and salam

practice.title: Questions and tasks
prompts: 💬 How many rak‘ahs does Asr have, and how are they divided? What is the niyyah for the fard of Asr?
📋 In your maktab notebook, draw a table of what we recite in each rak‘ah of Asr. Colour the rak‘ahs where we recite the same thing with the same colour, and compare it with Dhuhr.
💬 Talk with your muallim: Salah is a blessing and a way of thanking Allah for the many blessings I have!
